title: The Lament of the Stag (Ka Sur U Sier Lapalang)
cultural_context: The oldest and most revered tragedy in Khasi oral culture, serving as the archetype for all funeral wailing, laments (jamlu), and melancholic poetry. Tells of a young stag in the plains who longed for the sweet grass of the Khasi hills and died by hunter arrows.
lyrics_khasi:
Ko Lapalang phrang sngi jong nga,
Kum bating-shein u mankara!
Haba na nga me la khlad noh,
Dohnud sngewsih nga im suhsat.

Shong khop ha la ri them ri thor,
Bam da u khah bam da u nor!
Ngin bam da u jangew jathang,
Baroh shi lyiur baroh shi tlang!

Pynban kynrem na nga me khlad,
Sha Ri Khasi me la kiew krad!
U phlang ba thiang u la ring phai,
Ki thwei ba khuid ki la pynkai!

Wow! La shet ka tieh pongdeng,
Ia ka rynieng u kynrem reng!
Wow! La kjit u nam sarang,
Ia ka mynsiem u Lapalang!

Ha kliar Lum Shillong u la noh,
U khnam ba bih u la kem thoh!
Ummat ka kmie ki la shlei tuid,
Ki lum ki them ki la jaw ruid!

Ko khun baieit ba thiah ha madan,
Ym don shuh u ban pynkyndit kram!
Sah marwei nga ha kane ka sngi,
Ka nam jong me kan neh ha ri!
lyrics_english:
O Lapalang, light of my eyes and morning of my days,
With stately antlers like the majestic crown of the plains!
When thou didst depart from my maternal side,
My weeping heart was plunged into unending sorrow.

Abide quietly in our gentle lowlands and valleys,
Feeding upon the tall reed grasses and sweet water plants!
We shall eat our simple wild mountain herbs,
Through every monsoon summer and through every winter freeze!

Yet proud and noble, thou didst hasten away,
Climbing up into the crags of the sacred Khasi hills!
The tender scented grasses lured thee upward,
The pure crystal mountain pools beckoned thee astray!

Alas! The hunter's bowstring bent upon the ridge,
Aiming at the stately stature of the antlered prince!
Alas! The poisoned arrow pierced his side,
Drinking the mortal soul of young Lapalang!

Upon the summit of Mount Shillong he collapsed,
The venom of the iron shaft took hold upon his veins!
The tears of his grieving mother overflowed in torrents,
The crags and deep ravines wept and trickled in grief!

O beloved child resting motionless upon the field,
None remains to awaken thee from thy deep slumber!
Alone I linger upon this dark mountain day,
Yet thy renown shall live forever across our hills!

stanzas.title: Ka Jingrwai Kmie ha Ri Thor (Mother's Plea in the Plains)
stanzas.khasi:
Ko Lapalang phrang sngi jong nga,
Kum bating-shein u mankara!
Haba na nga me la khlad noh,
Dohnud sngewsih nga im suhsat.
Shong khop ha la ri them ri thor,
Bam da u khah bam da u nor!
stanzas.english: O Lapalang my firstborn star, antlered like the proud tree of the plain! Since thou hast departed from me, my heart lives in grieving anguish. Stay peacefully in our lowlands, eating reed-grass and river-greens!

stanzas.title: Ka Jingkiew sha Ri Lum (Ascent to the Khasi Hills)
stanzas.khasi:
Pynban kynrem na nga me khlad,
Sha Ri Khasi me la kiew krad!
U phlang ba thiang u la ring phai,
Ki thwei ba khuid ki la pynkai!
stanzas.english: Yet proud and majestic thou didst wander, climbing up to the crags of the Khasi hills! The sweet scented mountain grass lured thee, the crystal highland pools drew thee on!

stanzas.title: Ka Jingiap ha Lum Shillong (Death on Mount Shillong)
stanzas.khasi:
Wow! La shet ka tieh pongdeng,
Ia ka rynieng u kynrem reng!
Wow! La kjit u nam sarang,
Ia ka mynsiem u Lapalang!
stanzas.english: Alas! The hunter's bent bow betrayed the stature of the antlered prince! Alas! The poisoned iron arrow drank the mortal breath of Lapalang!

stanzas.title: Ka Ktien Khatduh (The Mother's Final Weeping)
stanzas.khasi:
Ko khun baieit ba thiah ha madan,
Ym don shuh u ban pynkyndit kram!
Sah marwei nga ha kane ka sngi,
Ka nam jong me kan neh ha ri!
stanzas.english: O darling child asleep upon the barren field, no one remains to wake thee now! Alone I am left on this dark earth, yet thy memory will echo forever through our land!

vocabulary.phrang sngi: Firstborn, dawn of the day, favorite child
vocabulary.kynrem reng: Magnificent branched antlers of a mature stag
vocabulary.nam sarang: Barbed iron hunting arrow with aconite venom
vocabulary.jangew jathang: Traditional indigenous wild medicinal edible greens
vocabulary.jamlu: Sacred funeral weeping and musical lamentation chant
